h: Making the O2 trip run smoothly
p: The O2 can be a very different place depending on when you go. On a quiet weekday morning it's calm and easy to get around. On a big concert or event night, thousands of people are heading the same way as you, the Tube gets rammed and the restaurants fill up. If you're bringing kids, a daytime slot on a non-event day is the stress-free option, so check what's on at the arena before you pick your time.

Once you're there, give yourself a cushion before your session starts. Check-in, harness fitting and the safety briefing all happen before the climbing does. Every climber needs a participation form, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s, and filling it in on the way saves time at the desk. There's usually a minimum age too, so have a look before booking.

On the walls, pace yourselves. It's tempting to sprint up the biggest challenge first, but arms tire fast. Start with something easy, build up, and keep the jumps for when everyone's confidence is flying. Phones are best left with a non-climber, who also gets the important job of filming.

Afterwards, the Thames Path runs right round the Greenwich Peninsula, a breezy riverside walk with views over to Canary Wharf. The Uber Boat by Thames Clippers runs from the pier by the arena into central London, which turns the journey home into a mini sightseeing cruise past Tower Bridge.
